Sara (CS): FYI opened from Acme support — customer reports embedding + rerank regressions after yesterday's runtime deploy. Top result irrelevant ~40% of the time, recall drop and latency tail increase. Posting repro snippets and perf traces below.

Maya (Support): Got the repro. Quick numbers: their test corpus (200 queries) recall@10 dropped 0.87 -> 0.62. P95 latency for embeddings + rerank up ~50ms. They use dedicated infra and set quantize=true in client.

Alex (ML): :eyes: Can you attach sample queries and the embeddings? Hypothesis: quantization mismatch between index vectors and runtime quantized embeddings OR cache eviction causing different prefixes. Need batch sizes, index format, and shard config.

Sara (CS): Sample (anonymized):
```json
{"query":"refund policy for enterprise plan","scores":[0.02,0.9,0.1],"ids":["doc3","doc1","doc2"]}
```
(really small excerpt but shows top result is weird)

Maya (Support): Repro steps they gave: call /v1/embeddings model=redwood-embed-v2-q4 batch_size=16, then rerank using cosine on our hosted vector DB. Index was built earlier with float16 vectors (no quant).

Alex (ML): If index is float16 while live queries are quantized (q4), distances can shift due to scale/zero-point changes. Quick local check shows L2 norms changed ~12% after q4 quantization on same vectors. That can reorder rankings.

Ben (PM): This looks product-facing and high impact. Acme is an enterprise customer under committed contract; sales flagged renewal risk. Jose, confirm escalation severity?

Jose (Sales): Confirmed. Relevance failures hitting legal doc search. Customer is unhappy; they asked for an ETA. We need clear mitigation path.

Ben (PM): Proposed triage path: (1) open RED-2137 with acceptance criteria: recall@10 >= 0.82 on their corpus + p95 latency < 120ms; (2) short-term mitigation: force float16 runtime for their org or provide a compatibility shim when index type != runtime quant type; (3) long-term: add automated deploy evals comparing quantized runtime vs index type. Sound ok?

Maya (Support): Agreed. I'll attach the full query corpus, perf traces, and raw request headers to the ticket. Header note: `X-Client-Org: acme-corp`.

Alex (ML): I'll run a sweep across q2/q4/q8 and float16 to quantify reordering. Early theory: per-dimension scale mismatch in q4 kernel when mixing with precomputed float16 index. If confirmed, quick patch: normalize vectors post-quant to preserve L2 norm before similarity calc.

Ben (PM): Marking P1 for Dedicated customer impact. I'll file RED-2137 and assign alex_ml + maya_support as owners. Jose to own comms with Acme. Sara please draft customer-facing note and workaround.

Sara (CS): Drafting note now: "We're investigating a compatibility issue between quantized embeddings and prebuilt indices that can reduce recall. Temporary workaround: set quantize=false for your runtime calls or reindex using quantized vectors. We're prioritizing a fix." Keeping it short for ACME.

ops-bot: Ticket RED-2137 created by ben_pm: https://redwood.atlassian/RED-2137 :eyes:

Ben (PM): Timeline suggestion: triage complete by EOD tomorrow, spec by Friday, patch next week. If triage shows config mismatch we can do org-level rollback same day.

Maya (Support): Added traces + sample set to RED-2137. Also included client headers and batch sizes.

Alex (ML): I'll post benchmark results in the ticket. If normalization fixes ordering, we can push a targeted runtime shim quickly. Also recommend we add a unit/regression test in the embedding pipeline to catch quant/index mismatches.

Ben (PM): Noted — adding product backlog item RED-2200: "embedding-compat-evals". Acceptance: automated regression alerts for quant/index mismatch on deploys.

Sara (CS): I'll update Acme with the temporary workaround and confirm they can test with quantize=false.

Ben (PM): Thanks everyone. Keep updates in RED-2137. If anything changes or Acme escalates to legal, ping #exec-ops.
